newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia said to cut spending, ease fiscal burden.
newsitem.headline: Croatia said to cut spending, ease fiscal burden.

text.p: Croatian government plans to cut public spending to ease the fiscal burden on the economy in the next three years, the daily newspaper Slobodna Dalmacija reported on Wednesday.
It quoted Finance Minister as saying government spending should gradually be reduced to between 46 and 47 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP).
The country's consolidated 1996 budget, including health and pension payouts, was planned at 53 percent of GDP. But this share should go down to 51 percent next year, Prka said.
He said the 1997 budget deficit would not exceed three billion kuna and would be covered mostly by foreign borrowing.
This year's GDP was projected at 99 billion kuna. There have been no forecasts yet for next year.
Croatia is to complete a radical fiscal reform in 1997 with the introduction of a 22-percent VAT to replace the existing turnover tax, imposed at a compounded rate of some 26 percent.
Prka said income and profit tax would also be reorganised to bring down overheads from the current 160 percent on top of the net wages.
"This proportion should be one kuna in net wages to one kuna in tax and other contributions," he added. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
